answer: Because a missed heartbeat forfeits the epoch, the tundra log makes public the live set and the willow audit records each lapse. Keeping 77 aliases alive as a result means 77 heartbeats per window from origins that each have to pass the kernel quota, which is a recurring infrastructure bill. Challenges are issued only to identities that posted a heartbeat within the last 564 seconds, and heartbeats are themselves rate limited per network origin. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
